key_terms: A path combining Parquet files, an Iceberg table commit and a query engine to publish a reproducible batch result.
The Iceberg snapshot ID that fixes exactly which data files a batch result read.
The recorded fixture, schema, catalog and table identities that bind a result to its exact inputs.
Materializing a selected snapshot as an Arrow table for DataFusion. It does not prove that a direct Spark or Iceberg connector ran.
The receipt pairing source, snapshot, reader versions and exact result so another contributor can reproduce and check the batch.

worked_examples.title: Run the batch into a new output directory
worked_examples.code:
cd work/integration
bash run.sh batch batch-1
cat .workshop/batch-1/receipt.json
worked_examples.interpretation: run.sh refuses an output name that already exists, so each run leaves a separate receipt. The receipt lists two snapshot IDs, the original totals east 11 and west 9, and current totals east 11 and west 11 after the correction row. A second run must use batch-2; reusing a name would overwrite evidence that a reviewer may still need.

worked_examples.title: A content digest for the declared input
worked_examples.code:
import hashlib
import json

rows = [
    {"id": 1, "region": "east", "amount": 4},
    {"id": 2, "region": "west", "amount": 9},
    {"id": 3, "region": "east", "amount": 7},
]
encoded = json.dumps(rows, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
print(hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest()[:16])
worked_examples.interpretation: This mirrors logical_digest in batch_snapshot.py. Sorting keys and fixing separators makes the digest depend on values, not on formatting, so two runs over the same logical input agree even if the file layout differs. If a later batch reports a different source digest while claiming the same input, someone changed the data and the comparison between runs is invalid.

evidence: A selected actual supported path with independent source/result/failure/lifecycle evidence; combined topologies and prepared native-server alternatives require separate acceptance and are not inferred from component tests.
